sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **End of British Paramountcy**: The Act formally ended British rule and paramountcy over the Indian princely states, lapsing all treaties and agreements effective August 15, 1947.
• **Creation of Two Dominions**: Provided for the creation of two independent dominions, India and Pakistan, from August 15, 1947, with complete legislative sovereignty.
• **Abolition of Viceroy Office**: Terminated the office of the Viceroy of India and provided for a Governor-General for each dominion, to be appointed on the advice of the respective dominion cabinet.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Assented to by the British Crown on July 18, 1947, giving merely one month for the monumental division of assets, armed forces, and administrative apparatus.

items.definition: The legal termination of British suzerainty over princely states, theoretically granting them absolute independence to join either dominion or stay separate.
A semi-autonomous status where the country is self-governing internally but retains the British Monarch as the nominal head of state (represented by the Governor-General) until January 26, 1950.
A boundary demarcation commission chaired by Sir Cyril Radcliffe charged with drawing international borders between India and Pakistan in Bengal and Punjab.
Empowered to make provisional orders for bringing the Act into effective operation and removing constitutional difficulties until March 31, 1948.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Partition Zones**: Punjab in the West and Bengal in the East were partitioned based on contiguous Muslim and non-Muslim majority districts.
• **Referendums & Accessions**: Sylhet in Assam, NWFP (North-West Frontier Province), and Sindh held referendums or legislative votes to determine accession to Pakistan.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Massive communal violence, refugee crisis, division of military and financial assets, administrative dislocation.
• **Policy Interventions**: Emergency cabinet committees, military evacuation organizations, and robust diplomatic integration by the States Department under Sardar Patel.

items.title: Mnemonic for Core Provisions of Independence Act
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'P-L-A-D' (Paramountcy Lapsed, Assemblies Sovereign, Dominions Two, Government Act of 1935 modified temporarily).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Paramountcy ends, Constituent assemblies become sovereign parliaments, Two dominions born, Govt of India Act 1935 serves as interim constitution.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly verifies correct statutory statements in multi-statement MCQs.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Dates: June 3 Plan -> July 18 Royal Assent -> August 15 Independence.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often states that India became a 'Republic' on August 15, 1947. This is incorrect. India remained a 'Dominion' with the British King as head of state until January 26, 1950, when the Constitution came into force.

Mains Value Addition: Emphasize how the Indian Independence Act 1947 was unique—it was a rare instance of an imperial power legislating its own withdrawal and peacefully transferring sovereignty through constitutional machinery.

keyTakeaways: The Indian Independence Act 1947 translated the June 3 Plan into statutory law, partitioning British India into India and Pakistan.
It ended British paramountcy over princely states, creating both an administrative vacuum and an integration challenge resolved by leaders like Sardar Patel.
It established absolute legislative sovereignty for the dominion parliaments and removed the veto power of the British Crown.
